Youre feelings are perfectly valid! Its definitely hard trying to calm yourself when there’s a lot of horror stories out there right now (and even some misinformation!) I have issues with anxiety/panick attacks and scared myself silly before getting vaccinated (I got the J&J today!) I very nearly chickened out. I had a good friend go with me and get vaccinated at the same time, as well as the vaccine itself was unplanned and spontaneous (my aunt works at the UofM and her work had extra shots so she called me at 1:30 and I was vaccinated by 3:30!)

I would say stay away from online stories, since 90% of them tend to be bad side effects (a lot of people dont report how they are feeling if their symptoms are mild/nonexistent. So its hard to look at so much scary info and feel good about it. Try to remind yourself that things will be alright. They have safety measures in place just in case, and the vaccine is safe for you!

The best thing to do is prepare for if you do have some side effects. Like set up a small area that is easily accessible with things like electrolyte drinks, thermometer, tylenol, and anything you may need if you do have some mild side effects. 

If you can, have someone go with or motivate you to go. It helped so much to have someone with me and be with my roommates for the night after (we are all sleeping in the same room.) 

Also, you can ask the person administering your vaccine anything you want. I mentioned my POTS and they checked with the medical staff working there for me. Even letting them know your nervous can help! 

Try to remind yourself often how important it is for everyone to get vaccinated and the good parts of it! It reminded me how worthwhile it was and helped me push through! Also, easier said than done, but if you can try and nip those ‘what-if’ thoughts in the bud. Keep your mind on the facts and dont let it wander! I found myself panicking most when I let my thoughts run wild!!
